newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS - Betting on a bottom in Cisco.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS - Betting on a bottom in Cisco.

text.p: Options activity in Cisco Systems Inc suggested some investors think the stock may be close to bottoming out.
Cisco shares peaked at 75-3/4 on January 24.
By about 1045 CST/1745 GMT Monday, the stock was down 1-1/4 at 50-1/8. Turnover was heavy at nearly 19 million shares. The stock opened at 49-1/8.
"Usually with an opening like that, you'd see people coming in to buy the volatility," Patrick Hamilton at LETCO said. "But what was interesting was we've seen the opposite.
"They came in and sold volatility," he said. "We had put sellers."
Hamilton said volatility in Cisco options rose briefly off the opening but quickly dropped back, sliding below Friday's close to the mid-50 region.
"It seems as though maybe these guys are thinking Cisco is reaching its bottom," he said, referring to the put sellers.
The most active puts included the March 50, with total volume of about 4,865 contracts and the March 45, with total volume of about 1,600.
Cisco options trade on the Chicago Board Options Exchange and the Pacific Stock Exchange.
Hamilton added that some call sellers emerged early in the session, most likely investors trying to get short, but that action had slowed.
The most active Cisco call was the April 55, which traded around 4,635. The March 50 and 55 calls also were busy.

From a chart perspective, the stock remains at least in a short term downtrend but investors betting on a bottom could use the options as part of a bottom-fishing strategy, Gregory Nie, a technical analyst at EVEREN Securities said.
